fr: Il habite à Paris depuis mars.
en: He has lived in Paris since March.
notes: Liaison links 'il' to 'habite', so the silent h glides right into the vowel sound with no pause.

fr: Elles arrivent à midi pile.
en: They arrive at exactly noon.
notes: The liaison z sound between 'elles' and 'arrivent' is easy to miss in fast speech but must be written.

fr: Vous avez deux enfants.
en: You have two children.
notes: Two liaisons chain together here, vous avez and deux enfants, both adding a z sound.

fr: On est en retard aujourd'hui.
en: We are late today.
notes: The liaison n sound after 'on' before 'est' must not be forgotten in writing.

fr: Nous avons un petit chat.
en: We have a small cat.
notes: Liaison turns 'nous avons' into one flowing sound, but the words stay separate on paper.

fr: Ils ont soif après le sport.
en: They are thirsty after sport.
notes: The liaison z sound linking 'ils' and 'ont' must be written as two separate words, never merged.

fr: Elle est ici depuis hier.
en: She has been here since yesterday.
notes: Liaison links 'est' to 'ici', producing a t sound that is never written as a separate letter.

fr: On a une grande maison.
en: We have a big house.
notes: The pronoun 'on' sounds identical to the verb form 'ont', so listen for the singular verb 'a' that follows.

fr: Elles sont contentes de partir.
en: They are happy to leave.
notes: 'Sont' is often confused by sound with the possessive word 'son'; here it is the plural verb être.

fr: Elle sait où il travaille.
en: She knows where he works.
notes: The relative pronoun 'où' is written with an accent to distinguish it from 'ou' meaning or.

fr: Je la vois tous les jours.
en: I see her every day.
notes: The object pronoun 'la' has no accent, unlike the adverb 'là', though both sound the same.

fr: Il se lave avant de sortir.
en: He washes up before going out.
notes: The reflexive pronoun 'se' sounds exactly like the demonstrative 'ce', so context decides the spelling.

fr: On aime bien ce restaurant.
en: We really like this restaurant.
notes: Even with liaison, 'on' must never be written as 'ont' since no plural subject appears here.

fr: Voici la ville où elle habite.
en: Here is the city where she lives.
notes: Do not drop the accent on 'où': without it the word means 'or', changing the meaning entirely.

fr: Je ne sais pas son nom.
en: I do not know his name.
notes: The unstressed e in 'je' and 'ne' almost disappears in speech, but both letters must still be written.

fr: Tu me dis toujours la vérité.
en: You always tell me the truth.
notes: The schwa in the object pronoun 'me' is barely pronounced but cannot be dropped in writing.

fr: Il te parle très gentiment.
en: He speaks to you very kindly.
notes: The pronoun 'te' keeps its silent-sounding e even though the vowel almost vanishes when spoken quickly.

fr: Elle le regarde avec un sourire.
en: She looks at him with a smile.
notes: Two schwas in a row, 'le' and 're', tend to merge in fast speech but stay as separate letters.

fr: Nous te remercions beaucoup.
en: We thank you very much.
notes: The pronoun 'te' before a consonant keeps its faint e sound, easy to skip when writing quickly.

fr: Je le vois chaque semaine.
en: I see him every week.
notes: Three weak schwa sounds in a row, je, le, se, can trick the ear into hearing fewer syllables than exist.

fr: Tu ne le connais pas encore.
en: You do not know him yet.
notes: The negation 'ne' and object pronoun 'le' both carry a faint schwa that must still be spelled out.

fr: On y va tout de suite.
en: We are going there right away.
notes: The nasal vowel in 'on' must not be confused with a simple 'o' sound when writing.

fr: Il en parle souvent avec nous.
en: He often talks about it with us.
notes: The pronoun 'en' has a nasal vowel that is distinct from the letter combination 'an' elsewhere.

fr: J'en veux encore un peu.
en: I want a bit more of it.
notes: The elided pronoun 'en' keeps its nasal sound even fused with 'j', so the n is never dropped.

fr: Nous en parlons rarement.
en: We rarely talk about it.
notes: The nasal pronoun 'en' following the liaison sound can be mistaken for part of the verb ending.

fr: Elles en ont besoin maintenant.
en: They need some of it now.
notes: Three nasal sounds cluster together here, en, ont, and besoin, so listen carefully for each pronoun boundary.

fr: On en mange souvent le dimanche.
en: We often eat some on Sundays.
notes: Two nasal pronouns, on and en, sit side by side and must both be captured in the spelling.

fr: Vous en avez assez pour ce soir.
en: You have enough of it for tonight.
notes: The nasal pronoun 'en' before the liaison 'avez' can blend together, but both parts stay written.

fr: Tu parles très bien anglais.
en: You speak English very well.
notes: The final s on 'parles' after the pronoun 'tu' is completely silent but must still be written.

fr: Ils parlent trop fort le soir.
en: They speak too loudly in the evening.
notes: The ending -ent on 'parlent' is silent, sounding identical to the singular form 'parle'.

fr: Elles chantent bien à l'école.
en: They sing well at school.
notes: The silent -ent ending hides the plural subject 'elles', so the pronoun alone signals the plural.

fr: Vous dites la vérité toujours.
en: You always tell the truth.
notes: The final s of 'dites' is never pronounced but is required in writing right after the pronoun 'vous'.

fr: Ils finissent leurs devoirs ensemble.
en: They finish their homework together.
notes: The silent -ent in 'finissent' can trick the ear into missing the plural pronoun 'ils'.

fr: Tu écoutes toujours la radio.
en: You always listen to the radio.
notes: The final s of 'écoutes' is never pronounced but is required in writing after 'tu'.

fr: Elles habitent près du marché.
en: They live near the market.
notes: The silent final -ent of 'habitent' is easy to forget when only the liaison sound is heard.

fr: J'aime beaucoup ce quartier.
en: I really like this neighborhood.
notes: The subject pronoun 'je' elides to j' before the vowel of 'aime', losing the e entirely.

fr: Je l'aime plus que tout.
en: I love him more than anything.
notes: The object pronoun 'le' elides to l' before the vowel in 'aime', merging into one sound.

fr: S'il vient, je suis content.
en: If he comes, I am happy.
notes: The conjunction 'si' elides to s' only before 'il' or 'ils', not before other pronouns like 'elle'.

fr: Elle l'appelle chaque soir.
en: She calls him every evening.
notes: The object pronoun 'le' or 'la' elides to l' before the vowel sound of 'appelle'.

fr: Je l'invite à mon anniversaire.
en: I am inviting him to my birthday.
notes: The elided pronoun l' hides whether it means 'him' or 'her', only context tells us.

fr: Qu'elle vienne, ça me fait plaisir.
en: That she is coming makes me happy.
notes: The conjunction 'que' elides to qu' before the pronoun 'elle', losing the silent e.

fr: Je n'aime pas ce film du tout.
en: I do not like this film at all.
ipa: /ʒə nɛm pa sə film dy tu/
notes: The negation 'ne' elides to n' before the vowel of 'aime', a common spot to forget the apostrophe.

fr: Il est content de son travail.
en: He is happy with his job.
notes: The masculine adjective 'content' has no extra letters, unlike its feminine form 'contente'.

fr: Elle est contente de son travail.
en: She is happy with her job.
notes: The silent final t in 'contente' only appears because the pronoun 'elle' is feminine.

fr: Il est fatigué après le sport.
en: He is tired after sport.
notes: The past participle used as adjective, 'fatigué', sounds identical whether written with or without a final e.

fr: Elle est fatiguée après le sport.
en: She is tired after sport.
notes: The silent added e in 'fatiguée' signals the feminine pronoun 'elle' though pronunciation stays the same.

fr: Ils sont prêts à partir maintenant.
en: They are ready to leave now.
notes: The masculine plural 'prêts' adds a silent s that must match the pronoun 'ils'.

fr: Elles sont prêtes à partir maintenant.
en: They are ready to leave now.
notes: The feminine plural ending -tes on 'prêtes' is pronounced the same as the masculine but spelled differently.

fr: Il est né à Lyon en mars.
en: He was born in Lyon in March.
ipa: /il ɛ ne a ljɔ̃ ɑ̃ maʁs/
notes: The past participle 'né' stays without an extra e because the subject pronoun 'il' is masculine.

fr: Je leur parle chaque matin.
en: I speak to them every morning.
notes: The indirect object pronoun 'leur' never takes an s, unlike the possessive adjective 'leurs'.

fr: Elle leur donne des conseils utiles.
en: She gives them useful advice.
notes: As a pronoun, 'leur' stays invariable even before a plural noun like 'conseils'.

fr: Nous leur écrivons une lettre.
en: We write them a letter.
notes: 'Leur' as a pronoun is spelled without a final s here, even though it means 'to them'.

fr: Il y pense souvent le soir.
en: He often thinks about it in the evening.
notes: The pronoun 'y' is a single silent-sounding letter that is easy to omit when writing quickly.

fr: Elle y va tous les samedis.
en: She goes there every Saturday.
notes: The short pronoun 'y' placed right before the verb is often skipped by ear in fast speech.

fr: Tu le lui donnes tout de suite.
en: You give it to him right away.
ipa: /ty lə lɥi dɔn tu də sɥit/
notes: Two pronouns, le and lui, stack before the verb and both must be written separately.

fr: Je te le dis sincèrement.
en: I am telling it to you sincerely.
notes: The double pronoun order te then le is fixed and both small words must appear in writing.

fr: Nous vous le montrons demain.
en: We will show it to you tomorrow.
notes: The schwa in the pronoun 'le' almost disappears in rapid speech, but the letter must still be written before the verb.

fr: Elle me le raconte souvent.
en: She often tells it to me.
notes: The pronoun pair me le is short and unstressed, making both words easy to drop by mistake.

fr: Il nous les montre avec fierté.
en: He shows them to us proudly.
notes: The pronoun 'les' is always pronounced without its final s, silent here just as in the article 'les'.

fr: Vous le savez déjà, je pense.
en: You already know it, I think.
notes: Both 'le' and 'je' carry a faint unstressed e sound that native speakers barely pronounce but writers must not omit.

fr: Voici la maison qu'il a achetée l'année dernière.
en: Here is the house he bought last year.
ipa: /vwa.si la mɛ.zɔ̃ kil a a.ʃə.te la.ne dɛʁ.njɛʁ/
notes: The past participle 'achetée' agrees with 'la maison', the direct object placed before the verb by the relative pronoun 'que'.

fr: J'ai vu la voiture qu'elle a vendue hier.
en: I saw the car that she sold yesterday.
ipa: /ʒe vy la vwa.tyʁ kɛl a vɑ̃.dy jɛʁ/
notes: Because 'que' refers back to the feminine 'voiture', the participle 'vendue' takes a silent added e.

fr: La lettre que je lui ai envoyée est arrivée.
en: The letter that I sent him has arrived.
ipa: /la lɛtʁ kə ʒə lɥi e ɑ̃.vwa.je ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve/
notes: The direct object 'lettre' comes before the verb, so 'envoyée' must agree even though 'lui' is indirect.

fr: Les fleurs qu'il m'a offertes sont magnifiques.
en: The flowers he gave me are beautiful.
ipa: /le flœʁ kil ma ɔ.fɛʁt sɔ̃ ma.ɲi.fik/
notes: The plural feminine agreement on 'offertes' matches 'fleurs', the preceding direct object introduced by 'que'.

fr: Je les ai vues au marché ce matin.
en: I saw them at the market this morning.
ipa: /ʒə le.z‿e vy o maʁ.ʃe sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: The pronoun 'les' placed before 'ai' forces the participle 'vues' to agree in gender and number.

fr: Elle a pris les clés et les a rangées.
en: She took the keys and put them away.
ipa: /ɛl a pʁi le kle e le.z‿a ʁɑ̃.ʒe/
notes: The second clause uses the pronoun 'les' before the verb, so 'rangées' agrees with the feminine plural clés.

fr: La chanson que nous avons écoutée était belle.
en: The song we listened to was beautiful.
ipa: /la ʃɑ̃.sɔ̃ kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ e.ku.te e.tɛ bɛl/
notes: The preceding feminine object 'chanson' triggers the silent e on 'écoutée' even though the ear hears nothing extra.

fr: Où sont les photos que tu as prises hier ?
en: Where are the photos you took yesterday?
ipa: /u sɔ̃ le fɔ.to kə ty a pʁiz jɛʁ/
notes: The relative pronoun 'que' refers to the plural 'photos', so 'prises' takes both the e and the s.

fr: Il a retrouvé la clé qu'il avait perdue.
en: He found the key that he had lost.
ipa: /il a ʁə.tʁu.ve la kle kil a.vɛ pɛʁ.dy/
notes: The pluperfect participle 'perdue' still agrees with the feminine 'clé' placed before it by 'que'.

fr: Ce sont les valises qu'ils ont oubliées à l'hôtel.
en: Those are the suitcases they forgot at the hotel.
ipa: /sə sɔ̃ le va.liz kil.z‿ɔ̃ u.bli.je a lo.tɛl/
notes: The plural feminine 'valises' forces 'oubliées' to carry both the silent e and the s ending.

fr: La décision qu'elle a prise nous a surpris.
en: The decision she made surprised us.
ipa: /la de.si.zjɔ̃ kɛl a pʁiz nu a syʁ.pʁi/
notes: 'Prise' agrees with the feminine 'décision', unlike the invariable masculine form 'pris'.

fr: Les invités que nous avons reçus sont partis tard.
en: The guests we hosted left late.
ipa: /le.z‿ɛ̃.vi.te kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ʁə.sy sɔ̃ paʁ.ti taʁ/
notes: The masculine plural 'reçus' still needs its silent added s to match 'invités' before the verb.

fr: Elle a téléphoné à sa mère hier soir.
en: She called her mother last night.
ipa: /ɛl a te.le.fɔ.ne a sa mɛʁ jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: The preposition 'à' carries an accent to distinguish it from the verb form 'a', even though both sound alike.

fr: Ils ont oublié leurs clés au bureau.
en: They forgot their keys at the office.
notes: 'Ont' from avoir sounds exactly like the pronoun 'on', so the plural subject 'ils' is the only clue.

fr: Son frère et sa sœur sont arrivés ensemble.
en: Her brother and sister arrived together.
ipa: /sɔ̃ fʁɛʁ e sa sœʁ sɔ̃.t‿a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃.sɑ̃bl/
notes: 'Sont' the verb and 'son' the possessive sound related but are never interchangeable in spelling.

fr: Il l'a vue au cinéma la semaine dernière.
en: He saw her at the cinema last week.
ipa: /il la vy o si.ne.ma la sə.mɛn dɛʁ.njɛʁ/
notes: 'L'a', meaning him or her plus avoir, sounds just like 'la' and 'là', so context alone tells them apart.

fr: Elle sait où ils vont partir en vacances.
en: She knows where they are going on vacation.
ipa: /ɛl sɛ u il vɔ̃ paʁ.tiʁ ɑ̃ va.kɑ̃s/
notes: The relative pronoun 'où' needs its accent to avoid being read as the conjunction 'ou'.

fr: Il s'est levé tôt ce matin.
en: He got up early this morning.
notes: 'S'est' in this reflexive past tense sounds identical to 'c'est', but only one fits a reflexive verb.

fr: Elle s'est habillée avant de partir.
en: She got dressed before leaving.
notes: Again 's'est' can be misheard as 'c'est', so recognizing the reflexive pronoun 'se' avoids the mix-up.

fr: On a fini le projet à temps.
en: We finished the project on time.
ipa: /ɔ̃ a fi.ni lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ a tɑ̃/
notes: The subject pronoun 'on' followed by 'a' must not be written as the plural verb form 'ont'.

fr: Ils vont où nous allons aussi.
en: They are going where we are going too.
notes: The relative pronoun 'où' keeps its accent even squeezed between two verb forms that sound similar.

fr: Elle l'a appelé dès qu'elle a pu.
en: She called him as soon as she could.
ipa: /ɛl la a.pə.le dɛ kɛl a py/
notes: 'L'a' here meaning him plus avoir is easily confused by ear with 'la' or 'là' in rapid speech.

fr: Ses parents sont partis tôt ce matin.
en: Her parents left early this morning.
ipa: /se pa.ʁɑ̃ sɔ̃ paʁ.ti to sə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: 'Sont' the auxiliary verb is a classic homophone trap next to the possessive 'ses', though unrelated in meaning.

fr: On ira au marché s'il fait beau.
en: We will go to the market if the weather is nice.
ipa: /ɔ̃ i.ʁa o maʁ.ʃe sil fɛ bo/
notes: The pronoun 'on' before the future verb 'ira' must stay separate from the homophone verb form 'ont'.

fr: Je l'ai vu hier au parc.
en: I saw him yesterday at the park.
notes: The object pronoun 'le' elides to l' before the vowel of 'ai', a spot often left unwritten by mistake.

fr: Elle m'a téléphoné ce matin.
en: She called me this morning.
notes: The pronoun 'me' elides to m' before the vowel of 'a', merging two short words into one sound.

fr: Il t'a écrit une longue lettre.
en: He wrote you a long letter.
notes: The elided pronoun t' hides whether the sentence uses 'te' or another form, so context matters.

fr: Nous l'avons attendu longtemps.
en: We waited for him a long time.
notes: The pronoun 'le' elides before 'avons', and the following liaison adds another sound to track.

fr: Je vais l'inviter à mon mariage.
en: I am going to invite him to my wedding.
notes: In futur proche the pronoun still elides right before the infinitive, here l'inviter.

fr: Elle va l'appeler dès son arrivée.
en: She is going to call him as soon as she arrives.
notes: The elided pronoun before the infinitive 'appeler' keeps the same rule as in the present tense.

fr: Ils vont s'installer ici bientôt.
en: They are going to settle here soon.
notes: The reflexive pronoun 'se' elides to s' before the vowel of the infinitive 'installer'.

fr: Je ne l'ai pas encore lu.
en: I have not read it yet.
notes: Two elisions appear close together, ne before l'ai, both required even in negative sentences.

fr: Elle ne l'a pas vu depuis longtemps.
en: She has not seen him for a long time.
ipa: /ɛl nə la pa vy də.pɥi lɔ̃.tɑ̃/
notes: The elided object pronoun l' sits right after 'ne', both apostrophes easy to miss when writing fast.

fr: Il va l'emmener au cinéma demain.
en: He is going to take her to the cinema tomorrow.
notes: The elided pronoun before 'emmener' can be mistaken for part of the verb itself when spoken fast.

fr: Nous avons attendu le bus ensemble.
en: We waited for the bus together.
notes: Two liaisons chain in 'nous avons attendu', each adding a z sound not shown by any extra letter.

fr: Vous avez oublié votre parapluie.
en: You forgot your umbrella.
notes: The liaison between 'vous' and 'avez' must be written even though it sounds like one word.

fr: Ils ont acheté une nouvelle voiture.
en: They bought a new car.
notes: Liaison links 'ils', 'ont', and 'acheté' in a chain of added sounds that stay silent letters on the page.

fr: Elles ont invité tous leurs amis.
en: They invited all their friends.
notes: The plural pronoun 'elles' triggers a z liaison before the vowel-starting verb 'ont'.

fr: Il va arriver dans une heure.
en: He is going to arrive in an hour.
notes: In futur proche no liaison links 'il' and 'va', but the following 'dans une' does add one.

fr: Elles vont écouter ce nouvel album.
en: They are going to listen to this new album.
notes: The liaison between 'vont' and 'écouter' adds a t sound that never appears as a separate written word.

fr: Nous en avons besoin tout de suite.
en: We need some of it right away.
notes: Multiple liaisons chain through 'nous en avons', each one a silent letter brought to life by sound.

fr: Vous en avez déjà parlé ensemble.
en: You have already talked about it together.
notes: The liaison chain here spans three words, vous, en, and avez, easy to under-hear as one syllable.

fr: Ils y sont allés hier après-midi.
en: They went there yesterday afternoon.
notes: The pronoun 'y' sits between two liaison points, ils y and sont allés, both required in writing.

fr: Elles y ont pensé toute la soirée.
en: They thought about it all evening.
notes: The pronoun 'y' triggers its own liaison before 'ont', stacking with the liaison after 'elles'.

fr: On en a parlé pendant des heures.
en: We talked about it for hours.
notes: Two nasal pronouns, on and en, sit together and both must be captured despite blending in speech.

fr: Il en a acheté plusieurs hier.
en: He bought several of them yesterday.
notes: The nasal pronoun 'en' before a vowel-starting verb keeps its full nasal sound, unlike a simple 'e'.

fr: Nous en avons discuté longuement.
en: We discussed it at length.
notes: The nasal vowel in 'en' can be swallowed by the surrounding liaisons if you are not listening carefully.

fr: On va en parler demain matin.
en: We are going to talk about it tomorrow morning.
notes: In futur proche the pronoun 'en' still keeps its nasal sound right before the infinitive.

fr: Elles en ont gardé un bon souvenir.
en: They kept a good memory of it.
notes: Three nasal sounds cluster in a row here, en, ont, and un, each needing its own careful spelling.

fr: On y est allé ensemble dimanche.
en: We went there together on Sunday.
notes: The nasal pronoun 'on' followed by 'y' can be mistaken as a single fused sound rather than two words.

fr: Vous en aurez besoin très bientôt.
en: You will need it very soon.
notes: The nasal pronoun 'en' keeps its distinct sound even when squeezed between two liaisons.

fr: Ils en ont profité tout le week-end.
en: They took advantage of it all weekend.
notes: The nasal vowels in en and ont line up back to back, a common spot for spelling slips.

fr: On en reparlera une autre fois.
en: We will talk about it again another time.
notes: The nasal pronoun 'en' before the future verb keeps its full sound despite the fast rhythm of speech.

fr: Elle en garde un très bon souvenir.
en: She keeps a very good memory of it.
ipa: /ɛl ɑ̃ ɡaʁd œ̃ tʁɛ bɔ̃ su.və.niʁ/
notes: The nasal pronoun 'en' must be written even though its vowel sound briefly merges with the verb that follows.

fr: Elle a pris les documents importants.
en: She took the important documents.
notes: The participle 'pris' ends in a silent s that is never pronounced after the vowel sound.

fr: Ils ont mis leurs affaires dans la voiture.
en: They put their things in the car.
notes: The participle 'mis' carries a silent final s, easy to forget since nothing is heard after the vowel.

fr: Elles ont dit la vérité sans hésiter.
en: They told the truth without hesitating.
notes: The participle 'dit' ends in a silent t that vanishes completely in pronunciation.

fr: Nous avons appris cette leçon ensemble.
en: We learned this lesson together.
notes: The final s of 'appris' is silent, the same trap as its shorter cousin 'pris'.

fr: Vous avez compris la consigne, je crois.
en: You understood the instructions, I think.
notes: The participle 'compris' ends in a silent s just like 'pris', with nothing heard after the final vowel.

fr: Elle a écrit une belle histoire.
en: She wrote a beautiful story.
notes: The participle 'écrit' hides a silent final t that the ear never catches.

fr: Ils ont conduit toute la nuit sans s'arrêter.
en: They drove all night without stopping.
ipa: /il.z‿ɔ̃ kɔ̃.dɥi tut la nɥi sɑ̃ sa.ʁɛ.te/
notes: The participle 'conduit' ends in a silent t, matching the pattern of other -uire verbs.

fr: Ils ont beaucoup voyagé cette année.
en: They traveled a lot this year.
notes: The final s of the pronoun 'ils' is silent on its own, only surfacing as a z sound through liaison.

fr: Elles ont pris une décision importante.
en: They made an important decision.
notes: Both the pronoun 'elles' and the participle 'pris' hide silent final consonants unless liaison bridges them.

fr: Vous avez dit vrai depuis le début.
en: You have been right from the start.
notes: The pronoun 'vous' ends in a silent s, heard only as the liaison z before the vowel of 'avez'.

fr: Je te le dirai demain sans faute.
en: I will tell it to you tomorrow without fail.
ipa: /ʒə tə lə di.ʁe də.mɛ̃ sɑ̃ fot/
notes: Three schwa sounds stack in je, te, le, each barely audible but all required in writing.

fr: Il me l'a promis la semaine dernière.
en: He promised it to me last week.
ipa: /il mə la pʁɔ.mi la sə.mɛn dɛʁ.njɛʁ/
notes: The pronoun 'me' before the elided 'l'a' carries a weak schwa that must still appear in spelling.

fr: Tu me le rendras la semaine prochaine.
en: You will give it back to me next week.
ipa: /ty mə lə ʁɑ̃.dʁa la sə.mɛn pʁɔ.ʃɛn/
notes: The pronoun cluster me le both carry near-silent schwas that are easy to drop when writing fast.

fr: Nous te le proposons volontiers.
en: We are offering it to you gladly.
notes: The double pronoun te le both keep their faint schwa vowel despite sounding almost swallowed.

fr: Elle te le dira si tu insistes.
en: She will tell it to you if you insist.
ipa: /ɛl tə lə di.ʁa si ty ɛ̃.sist/
notes: The unstressed pronouns te and le blur together in speech but remain two separate written words.

fr: Je ne te le cache pas du tout.
en: I am not hiding it from you at all.
ipa: /ʒə nə tə lə kaʃ pa dy tu/
notes: Four schwa sounds appear in a row here, je, ne, te, le, testing how carefully you track each syllable.

fr: Il te le rendra dès que possible.
en: He will give it back to you as soon as possible.
ipa: /il tə lə ʁɑ̃.dʁa dɛ kə pɔ.sibl/
notes: The pronoun pair te le sits right before the future verb, both schwas easy to underhear.

fr: Tu ne me le dis jamais franchement.
en: You never tell it to me frankly.
ipa: /ty nə mə lə di ʒa.mɛ fʁɑ̃.ʃə.mɑ̃/
notes: Three schwa vowels crowd together in ne, me, le, a common spot to lose a syllable when writing.

fr: Elle ne te le donnera pas ce soir.
en: She will not give it to you tonight.
ipa: /ɛl nə tə lə dɔ.nə.ʁa pa sə swaʁ/
notes: Multiple weak schwas across ne, te, le, and even donnera can make the sentence sound shorter than it is written.

fr: Il ne va pas leur parler ce soir.
en: He is not going to talk to them tonight.
ipa: /il nə va pa lœʁ paʁ.le sə swaʁ/
notes: In futur proche negation, 'leur' stays invariable and is placed right before the infinitive, never taking an s.

fr: Je ne le lui ai pas encore donné.
en: I have not given it to him yet.
ipa: /ʒə nə lə lɥi e pa ɑ̃.kɔʁ dɔ.ne/
notes: The pronoun order le then lui is fixed and both must appear even squeezed inside the negation.

fr: Elle va leur écrire une carte postale.
en: She is going to write them a postcard.
ipa: /ɛl va lœʁ e.kʁiʁ yn kaʁt pɔs.tal/
notes: The indirect pronoun 'leur' before the infinitive never becomes 'leurs', even meaning to several people.

fr: Nous allons le leur expliquer calmement.
en: We are going to explain it to them calmly.
notes: The order le leur before an infinitive keeps both short pronouns distinct in the spelling.

fr: Vous n'allez pas nous les rendre aujourd'hui.
en: You are not going to give them back to us today.
ipa: /vu na.le pa nu le ʁɑ̃dʁ o.ʒuʁ.dɥi/
notes: The pronoun pair nous les must stay in this fixed order right before the infinitive verb.

fr: Ils vont te le rendre très bientôt.
en: They are going to give it back to you very soon.
ipa: /il vɔ̃ tə lə ʁɑ̃dʁ tʁɛ bjɛ̃.to/
notes: The two pronouns te and le placed before the infinitive both need separate letters despite their brief sound.

fr: Elle ne va pas y retourner cette année.
en: She is not going to go back there this year.
ipa: /ɛl nə va pa i ʁə.tuʁ.ne sɛt a.ne/
notes: The pronoun 'y' keeps its place right before the infinitive even inside a negative futur proche.

fr: Nous n'allons pas en discuter maintenant.
en: We are not going to discuss it now.
notes: The pronoun 'en' is placed directly before the infinitive, staying a single letter easy to drop in fast writing.

fr: Il va me la présenter demain soir.
en: He is going to introduce her to me tomorrow evening.
ipa: /il va mə la pʁe.zɑ̃.te də.mɛ̃ swaʁ/
notes: The order me la before the infinitive is fixed, unlike le lui which reverses the pronoun order.

fr: Elles vont nous en parler bientôt.
en: They are going to talk to us about it soon.
notes: The pronoun pair nous en sits before the infinitive, both short words required despite the fast rhythm.
